news.title: Infantino set to receive World Cup win but loses Italy's support
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has received a big win with UEFA backing off its World Cup threat. UEFA is set to backtrack on its threat to boycott all FIFA tournaments ahead of next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland. UEFA has sought the withdrawal of FIFA boss Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plan and assurances that similar plans will not be pursued again. Italy has withdrawn its support for Infantino's candidacy at next year's FIFA presidential election, with France to consider its stance as well.

news.title: Uefa to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
news.lede: Uefa has received guarantees after ill-fated Infantino plan. European sides will go to under-20 Women’s World Cup. Uefa is to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. European teams have been cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.

news.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi is the most promising defensive midfielder in the world - but Rodri's replacement won't fix all of Enzo Maresca's problems at Man City: GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer window
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: UEFA ready to drop FIFA boycott threat after assurances private World Cup sell-off plan won’t return
news.lede: UEFA is reportedly ready to call off its threatened boycott of FIFA competitions after receiving assurances that Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other major tournaments to private investors will not be brought back. Football News: UEFA prepares to lift its threatened boycott against FIFA after receiving assurances that the controversial selling of World Cup stakes to private investors will not be revived. This decision aims to ensure that upcoming FIFA tournaments proceed without disruption, although pressure on FIFA President Gianni Infantino continues to escalate.

news.title: Uefa to announce World Cup boycott decision tomorrow
news.lede: UEFA will lift its threat to boycott FIFA after Italy withdrew its support for the world football body's president, Gianni Infantino. UEFA is expected to conclude at a meeting in Monaco tomorrow that the conditions for lifting the boycott have been met, Reuters has learned. Italy withdraws support for Infantino amid disputes over FIFA governance. In July, FIFA withdrew a proposal to sell the World Cup to private investors after all 55 UEFA members agreed to a boycott.

news.title: UEFA set to lift FIFA boycott threat after investor plan shelved
news.lede: UEFA's Executive Committee is expected to formalize the withdrawal of its boycott threat against FIFA competitions on Thursday after securing assurances that the governing body will not revive plans to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors, according to the BBC. The dispute erupted in late July when FIFA unveiled its FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, which sought to create a commercial entity controlling rights to the World Cup and other tournaments with private investment taking stakes. UEFA's 55 member associations unanimously voted on July 30 to boycott FIFA competitions unless the plan was scrapped entirely and guarantees were provided against future privatization attempts, with FIFA withdrawing the proposal on August 1 following widespread criticism from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF.

news.title: Jaipur’s Royal Football Club captain Rannanjay Singh Bhati selected for India U-15 FIFA World Cup camp tr
news.lede: Jaipur: Rannanjay Singh Bhati, captain of Royal Football Club, Jaipur’s Under-15 team and one of the club’s promising young footballers, has been selected for the trials of the India U-15 FIFA World Cup camp. The trials are being conducted by the All India Football Federation (AIFF) in Bengaluru.Royal Football Club’s head coach, Narendra Singh Rathore, said that under Rannanjay Singh Bhati’s captaincy, the club won the Rajasthan U-15 Youth League 2025 title this year and also qualified for the AIFF Youth League 2026. His leadership qualities, discipline and footballing ability have played an important role in the team’s success.Club director Dr Dilip Singh Chundawat said that Rannanjay Singh Bhati has been undergoing regular training at Royal Football Club for the past two years.
